messages:
Alex P.: quick one — prototyping a Policy Authoring mini-flow for routing by customer-tier + region. thinking about how fallback variants should behave when a tier hits quota. anyone have strong opinions on semantics?
Maria S.: high level — prefer deterministic fallback order (explicit list) + a soft-quota window so pro users don't flip to low-quality models mid-request.
Jordan H.: UX: console needs to show the effective route (model + region) and a single-line reason why it selected fallback, e.g., "fallback: quota exceed -> used distill-v2". users hate guessing.
Sam L.: telemetry: we should emit a metric per request: route_selected, fallback_reason, original_model, final_model, tenant_tier. That lets us alert on regression. also include token_delta estimate.
Tay: policy question — do we want per-tenant override to opt-out of fallbacks? enterprise might want guaranteed model or hard deny. free/pro should be able to fallback automatically.
Alex P.: exactly — thinking of 3 modes at policy-level: allow_fallback (true/false), fallback_order (array), soft_quota_window_seconds (int). default: allow_fallback true for free/pro, false for enterprise.
Maria S.: API sketch would be helpful. quick example?
Alex P.: pasted quick schema draft:
```json
{
  "tier": "pro",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "allow_fallback": true,
  "fallback_order": ["distill-v2", "cpu-quantized"],
  "soft_quota_window_seconds": 120,
  "quota_policy": {"tokens_per_minute": 10000, "grace_percentage": 0.15}
}
```
Jordan H.: console preview: show a diff view when editing fallback_order. show estimated latency/cost for each variant inline. small sparkline of recent fallback rate would be 🔥
Sam L.: on enforcement — two options: 1) hard reject when quota exceeded (HTTP 429) 2) soft-fallback during soft window (degrade to next model) 3) queued retry. need to pick default per tier.
Tay: recommended defaults: free -> soft-fallback + queue disabled, pro -> soft-fallback + queue enabled, enterprise -> hard reject unless tenant explicitly allows fallback.
Alex P.: question for infra — how to implement kv-cache consistency across variants? if you switch variant mid-request you lose kv-cache optimizations. we should probably avoid mid-request model swaps unless variants share cache format.
Sam L.: agree. emit an event when a request hits fallback and if KV cache was missed. that will help quantify cost.
Maria S.: console control: add a toggle "allow mid-request variant swap (unsafe)" with a big warning. default off.
Jordan H.: also need rollout flags for experiments: e.g., gradual fallback activation at 1/5/25/100% of affected tenants. add a small CTA in console to run evals on fallback models before flipping.
Alex P.: TL;DR action items: 1) Alex to push API schema PR with the fields above. 2) Sam to add telemetry proto for route_selected + fallback_reason. 3) Jordan to mock console diff + rollout UX. 4) Tay to write default tier mapping doc.
DevOpsBot: pipeline:policy-schema-pr triggered by Alex P. — build started (job-4721). :rocket:
Maria S.: thanks all. if anyone wants to pair on the PR ping me.
Alex P.: will ping @MariaS and @SamL tomorrow for 30m review. thanks!
